correctness.rationale: The base-b positions of ones are the binary index digits recoded as digits 0 and b−1. Taking consecutive differences proves exact zero-gap lengths (b−2)b^{v2(i)}. Every palindrome with at least two ones must center on a gap; valuations v2(i±h)=v2(h) for h<2^{v2(i)} give a mirrored central block mu_b^{j+1}(1), and the next neighboring gaps of lengths g_{j+1} and >=g_{j+2} give a sharp maximal symmetric extension (achieved at gap index 3*2^j). One-centered palindromes have at most 2(b−2)+1 symbols, and all-zero words occur at every length. Central zero-gap lengths distinguish different nonzero palindrome words. These prove the claimed formula and uniform sharp bound. Standalone verify.py returned VERIFY_OK on 745 (base,length) tests with independent digit, gap and core checks; tests are explicitly nonproof regressions.

value.rationale: The two-end Cantor sequence is a natural self-similar automatic word family; its palindromic-factor complexity is a standard combinatorial invariant. The theorem gives a complete and explicit all-length, all-base b>=4 function, a sharp universal three-valued bound with all three values attained, and a structural description via 2-adic gap axes and substitution cores. General automatic regularity, classical b=3 maximal symmetry, and k-Abelian factor complexity do not determine these exact quantitative transitions. The result is not an arbitrarily selected finite example.
